# E0-B MB0 — Executable Contract Table

**8 October 2026 · generated by `e0b_contracts.py` · development artefact, not confirmatory**

This table comes before any interpretation of S1h and before any margin is set (v2.2 Appendix C). Each row names an encoder, the exact variables it observes, a consumer, and the exact variables that consumer observes. The value is computed from those same variables. Two rules make this enforceable in code:
- An ideal encoder emits \(E[\text{target} \mid \text{declared inputs}]\). It cannot use an input its contract withholds.
- A consumer earns the Bayes-optimal value given its declared observations.

## Declared Contracts

| Role | Observes | Never observes |
|---|---|---|
| φ encoder (Shea candidate) | \(o, R, T\) (via θ access), mapping access (oracle \(f\) **or** trace MAP \(\hat f\)), κ | \(X, N\), mapping parameters \((w,b)\) |
| Q encoder (B1-action-value) | identical to the φ encoder | identical |
| acceptance consumer | M, R, κ | \(X\) |
| relay consumer (correctness-paid) | M, R | κ, \(X\) |
| traces | k i.i.d. report samples per public input; \(X, N, T\) unobserved; ties uniform | — |

"Mapping oracle" rows give the encoder the true \(f(o)\). They are oracle subproblems and are labelled as such. Achievable rows use \(\hat f\) from k traces.
